answer: Copying the same citations across 204 aliases hence forfeits the authoring cost 204 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the beacon index resolves every citation against the vertex checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the echo audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 39 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
